subject: Polity
description: Covers Finance Commission, CAG, Attorney General.

questions.stem: Which constitutional body is responsible for deciding the distribution of the net proceeds of taxes between the Centre and the States?

options.option_text: The Finance Commission
The NITI Aayog
The GST Council
The Reserve Bank of India

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Under Article 280, the Finance Commission is a quasi-judicial body constituted by the President every five years. Its core duty is to recommend the distribution of the net proceeds of taxes between the Centre and the states (Vertical Devolution) and among the states themselves (Horizontal Devolution).
DECOY BUSTING: NITI Aayog is a policy think tank, not a constitutional body, and does not distribute funds. The GST Council determines GST rates. The RBI handles monetary policy, not tax devolution.
EXAM INSIGHT: The 15th Finance Commission (chaired by N.K. Singh) recommended that 41% of the divisible pool of taxes be transferred to the states (down from 42% due to the creation of the UTs of J&K and Ladakh).

questions.stem: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India, the supreme audit institution of the country, is appointed under which Article of the Constitution?

options.option_text: Article 148
Article 76
Article 280
Article 324

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Article 148 provides for an independent office of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India. He is the head of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department and the guardian of the public purse. He audits all receipts and expenditures of the Government of India and the state governments.
DECOY BUSTING: Article 76 provides for the Attorney General of India (highest law officer). Article 280 provides for the Finance Commission. Article 324 provides for the Election Commission of India.
EXAM INSIGHT: To ensure total independence, the CAG can only be removed from office by the President on the same grounds and in the same manner as a judge of the Supreme Court (requiring a special majority in Parliament).

questions.stem: Who is the highest law officer in India, appointed by the President to give advice to the Government of India upon legal matters?

options.option_text: Attorney General of India
Solicitor General of India
Chief Justice of India
Law Minister of India

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Attorney General of India (Article 76) is the highest law officer in the country. Appointed by the President, he must be a person qualified to be appointed as a judge of the Supreme Court. It is his duty to advise the GOI upon legal matters and to appear on behalf of the GOI in all cases in the Supreme Court in which the GOI is concerned.
DECOY BUSTING: The Solicitor General is subordinate to the Attorney General and assists him; the SG is a statutory post, not a constitutional one. The Chief Justice is the head of the judiciary, not a government lawyer. The Law Minister is a political appointee.
EXAM INSIGHT: The Attorney General has the unique privilege to speak and take part in the proceedings of BOTH Houses of Parliament (or any joint sitting), but he does NOT have the right to vote.

questions.stem: Which Article of the Constitution vests the superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission of India?

options.option_text: Article 324 (Superintendence and control of elections)
Article 315 (Establishment of Public Service Commissions)
Article 280 (Constitution of the Finance Commission)
Article 148 (Comptroller and Auditor General of India)

questions.explanation: Article 324 vests superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and conduct of elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, and offices of President and Vice-President in the Election Commission. Article 315, the most tempting distractor, establishes Public Service Commissions — another constitutional body — leading students to mix up the article numbers.

questions.stem: The Chief Election Commissioner of India can be removed from office only in a manner similar to the removal of which constitutional authority?

options.option_text: A Judge of the Supreme Court of India (by parliamentary address)
The President of India (by impeachment in both Houses of Parliament)
The Comptroller and Auditor General (by a Presidential removal order)
The Attorney General, who serves entirely at the pleasure of the President

questions.explanation: Article 324(5) explicitly states that the CEC shall not be removed except in like manner and on like grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court — i.e., on an address by each House of Parliament supported by a special majority. Option B (President) is wrong because the President is removed by impeachment, which is a different and more elaborate procedure; the SC judge removal method used for the CEC is technically an 'address', not an 'impeachment'.

questions.stem: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes received independent constitutional status through which provision, separating it from the earlier combined Special Officer framework?

options.option_text: Article 338, amended by the 89th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003
Article 338-A, inserted specifically for Scheduled Tribes welfare matters
Article 339, granting Union control over scheduled areas administration
Article 340, authorising appointment of a Backward Classes Commission

questions.explanation: The 89th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 bifurcated the original Article 338 (which housed a single Special Officer for both SCs and STs) into Article 338 (National Commission for Scheduled Castes) and Article 338-A (National Commission for Scheduled Tribes). Article 338-A is the most common wrong answer because students reverse which article number applies to which community after the bifurcation.

questions.stem: A member of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) appointed by the President shall hold office until attaining which age, as prescribed under Article 316(2)?

options.option_text: 65 years, or a tenure of 6 years, whichever comes earlier
62 years, or a tenure of 6 years (the State PSC superannuation limit)
60 years, which is the standard superannuation age in Union civil services
58 years, extendable by Presidential order for a further two-year term

questions.explanation: Article 316(2) prescribes that a UPSC member holds office for six years from appointment or until attaining the age of 65, whichever is earlier. The age of 62 applies to State Public Service Commission members — a very common confusion in exams. The general civil service retirement age of 60 is irrelevant here, as UPSC members are constitutional authorities with separately prescribed tenure, not ordinary government servants.

questions.stem: Under Article 280(1), the Finance Commission constituted by the President must mandatorily consist of which composition?

options.option_text: A Chairperson and four other members, making five in total
A Chairperson and five other members, making six in total
A Chairperson and three other members, making four in total
A Chairperson and six other members, making seven in total

questions.explanation: Article 280(1) explicitly mandates the Finance Commission shall consist of a Chairman and four other members appointed by the President — five persons in total. The number is fixed in the Constitution itself, while qualifications of members are left to Parliament by law under Article 280(1)(b). Students frequently guess six by confusing it with other multi-member bodies or by miscounting the provision.

questions.stem: Which constitutional restriction placed on the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India is stricter than the restriction placed on retired Supreme Court judges?

options.option_text: The CAG is permanently barred from any government office after retirement
The CAG's reports must receive Presidential approval before parliamentary tabling
The CAG can initiate suo motu audit of autonomous bodies without executive referral
The CAG is appointed jointly by the President and Prime Minister in consultation

questions.explanation: Article 148(4) provides an absolute post-retirement bar: after ceasing to hold office, the CAG shall not be eligible for further office under the Government of India or any State. Retired Supreme Court judges face no such bar and routinely head commissions, tribunals, or inquiry committees. This stronger restriction insulates the CAG from executive influence by removing any incentive for career-friendly audit outcomes. Option B is wrong because the CAG submits reports to the President (or Governor), who then causes them to be laid before Parliament — there is no 'Presidential approval' requirement.

questions.stem: The Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT), established under the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985 pursuant to Article 323-A, explicitly excludes which of the following categories from its service-matter jurisdiction?

options.option_text: Members of the Armed Forces governed by separate service legislation
All India Service officers who are posted to Central government ministries
Central civil service employees facing major-penalty departmental proceedings
Railway employees whose service disputes relate to seniority or promotions

questions.explanation: Section 14 of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985 explicitly excludes members of any force constituted under the Army Act, Navy Act, or Air Force Act from CAT's jurisdiction. Their service disputes are adjudicated by the Armed Forces Tribunal established under the Armed Forces Tribunal Act, 2007. All India Service officers (B), Central civil service employees (C), and Railway employees (D) all fall within CAT's jurisdiction. Candidates typically err by assuming 'any government employee = CAT jurisdiction' without knowing the Armed Forces carve-out.
